look_here_first: Think gray-hairy rhizomatous gaura: narrow foliage and stems are usually covered with appressed gray hairs, and the small pale flowers fade pink to scarlet.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: gray appressed hairs on foliage and stems

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small white to pink flowers often aging scarlet

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fruit with thick stipe widest toward base

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: dry prairie and rocky grassland habit

lookalikes.differences: Compared with O. sinuosa, O. suffrutescens is usually much grayer and hairier. Mature fruit structure is especially useful.
